sentences.text:
Avunoori Suguna vs Sayyad Mahaboob on 10 January, 2025
 Hon'Ble Smt.Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.88 of 2022
Judgment:

1. Dissatisfied with the compensation amount awarded by the Family Court Judge -cum- Additional District Judge, Karimnagar, in M.V.O.P.No.330 of 2014, dated 09.10.2019, the claim petitioners in the said M.V.O.P. preferred the present Appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Family Court Judge -cum- Additional District Judge, Karimnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the learned Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the claim petitioners, who are the wife, daughters and parents of Late Avunoori Swamy (hereinafter be referred as 'the deceased'), filed a petition under Section 166 (1)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- from the respondents on account of the death of the deceased in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.01.2014.

It is stated by the petitioners that on 12.01.2014 during morning hours, when the deceased was proceeding to Peddapalli to attend his work as driver on the Tractor Bearing No.AP-07-G- 4564 for cutting trees, on the way at about 10.00 AM, when he reached at the outskirts of Sabbitham Village, in the meantime, a Lorry Bearing No.AP-28-V-6160 which came from Peddapalli towards Adavi Srirampur side and which was MGP,J driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at high speed, dashed the tractor of the deceased with great force while overtaking the said Tractor.

As a result, the deceased sustained severe injuries on his Head and on vital parts of his body and immediately, he was shifted to the Hospital in 108 Ambulance and at about 10.30 A.M., he succumbed to injuries on the way to Hospital at Raghavapoor Village.
4.
Based on a complaint, Police of Basanthnagar Police Station, Karimnagar District, registered a case in Crime No.8 of 2014 under Section 304-A IPC.

It is stated by the petitioners that the deceased was 38 years old at the time of accident and he was hale and healthy and used to earn Rs.8,000/-
per month by working as a Driver on the Tractor Bearing No.AP-07-G-4564 and used to contribute his earnings for maintenance, welfare and development of his family.
Due to unfortunate death of the deceased, the petitioners lost their support, became destitute and were put to mental agony and shock.
Hence, filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.14,00,000/- against the Respondents.
5. Before the Tribunal, respondent No.5 remained ex-parte and Respondent Nos.1 to 4 entered appearance and filed their counters denying the material averments made in the MGP,J petition.

Respondent Nos.1 & 2/Driver and Owner of Lorry Bearing No.AP-28-V-6160, stated in their counter that Police of Basathnagar Police Station, Karimnagar District, registered a false case in Crime No.8 of 2014 under Section 304-A IPC and also filed false charge sheet against respondent No.1 to claim compensation and that there was no negligence on part of respondent No.1 in driving the lorry and that the compensation claimed is excess and exorbitant and hence prayed to dismiss the claim against them.

1 6.

entities.text: Police of Basathnagar Police Station, Karimnagar District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Respondent Nos.3 & 4/United Insurance Company rep. by its Manager and Branch Manager filed its counter contending that the owner of the crime Lorry failed to inform to the respondent- Company about the accident and copy of FIR as provided under Section 158(6) of M.V.Act, 1988.

Therefore, they cannot be held liable to indemnify the owner of the crime vehicle and hence prayed to dismiss the claim against the Insurance Company.
7.

Based on the pleadings made by both parties, the learned Tribunal had framed the following issues for conducting Trial:-
(i) Whether the pleaded accident took place on 12.01.2014 at 10.00 hours at the outskirts of Sabitham Village due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry baring No.AP-28-V-6160 driven by MGP,J R1 came from Peddapalli towards Adavi Srirampur side and dashed to the Tractor Bearing No.AP-07-G-4564 as result of which the deceased Avunoori Swamuy, who was going to Gundaram Village from Peddapalli for cutting trees by driving the said tractor received severe injuries on head and other parts of his body and died on the way while shifting to Hospital?
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation?
If so, to what amount and from of the respondent?
(iii) To what relief?
8. Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the petitioners, PWs.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A1 to A7 were marked.
On behalf of respondents, no oral evidence was adduced, however, Ex.B1-Copy of Insurance Policy was marked with consent.

9. After considering the evidence and documents available on record, the learned Tribunal had partly-allowed the claim petition of the petitioners by awarding compensation of Rs.9,79,000/-
along with costs and interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit payable by respondent Nos.1, 3 to 5 jointly and severally.
Having not satisfied with the said compensation amount, the claim petitioners preferred the present Appeal seeking enhancement of the same.
MGP,J 10.
Heard Sri T.Ramulu, learned counsel for the appellants/claim petitioners as well as Sri A.Rama Krishna Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for respondent Nos.3 & 4/Insurance Company.
Perused the record.

11. The contentions of the learned counsel for appellants as stated in the grounds of Appeal are that the learned Tribunal ought to have taken income of the deceased @ Rs.8,000/- per month by considering Ex.A7-Salary Certificate of the deceased and ought to have awarded future prospects to the income of the deceased and also ought to have awarded parental consortium to his two children,
spousal consortium and filial consortium to the parents of the deceased and also ought to have Avunoori Suguna vs Sayyad Mahaboob on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158820683/
2 awarded more interest @ 12% per annum instead of 7.5% per annum and hence prayed to allow the Appeal by enhancing the compensation.
12.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/Insurance Company contended that the learned Trial Court, after considering all the aspects, had rightly awarded reasonable compensation and interference of this Court is unwarranted.
13.
Now the point that arises for determination is, Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?

MGP,J POINT:-
14.

A perusal of the record shows that petitioner No.1/wife of the deceased was examined as PW1 and filed an affidavit in lieu of her chief examination and reiterated the contents made in the claim petition.

As she is not an eye witness to the incident, she got examined PW2, an eye witness to the incident who deposed that on 12.01.2014, when he was going to Peddapalli from his village in order to attend some personal work, on the way at the outskirts of Sabbitham Village, he noticed one lorry bearing No.AP-28-V- 6160 coming from Peddapalli towards Adavi Srirampur and which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner at a high speed, dashed the Tractor of the deceased due to which, the said Tractor turned turtle and the driver of the said tractor fell down and the crime lorry was stopped at a distance of 200 yards away from the place of accident and the deceased sustained severe bleeding injuries on his head and other parts of the body.

Immediately, he along with the mother of the deceased shifted the deceased to Hospital in 108 Ambulance, but on the way,
the deceased succumbed to injuries.

15. The evidence of PW3/owner of the Tractor Bearing No.AP-07-G-4564 discloses that the deceased used to work as driver on the subject Tractor and was being paid an amount MGP,J of Rs.8,000/- per month towards salary which is also evident from Ex.A7-Salary Certificate.
16. Apart from oral evidence, the petitioners also filed documentary evidence under Exs.A1 to A7.
Ex.A1 is the FIR registered by Basanthnagar Police in Crime No.8 of 2014, conducted investigation and filed charge sheet under Ex.A2.
Ex.A3 is the inquest report.
Ex.A4 is the post-mortem examination report which discloses that the cause of death of the deceased was due to 'Head injury'.
Ex.A5 is the copy of Form 54-Accident Information Report.
Ex . A6
is the Motor Vehicle Inspector report.
Ex.A7 is the salary certificate issued by M.R.Prasad of Goureddypet Village, Peddapalli Mandal.

17. Therefore, from the evidence of PWs 1 to 3 coupled with the documentary evidence marked under Exs.A1 to A7, it is clear that the death of the deceased was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of crime vehicle i.e., Lorry bearing No.AP-28-V-6160 which is having valid insurance as on the date of accident as per Ex.B1.
18.
On the other hand, the respondents did not adduce any oral evidence except marking Ex.B1-Insurance Policy with consent.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the learned Tribunal ought to have taken the evidence of PW3 into consideration and ought to have fixed the income of the deceased @
Rs.8,000/- per month as per Ex.A7-Salary Certificate and ought to have awarded future prospects.

20. In this regard, this Court has perused the evidence of PW3/Owner of Tractor bearing No.AP-07-G-4564 which discloses that the deceased used to work as Driver on PW3's Tractor prior to his death and PW3 used to pay Rs.8,000/- per month towards salary of the deceased and Ex.A7 is the Salary certificate issued by him.

Hence, this Court, taking into consideration the evidence of PW3 coupled with Ex.A7- Salary Certificate is inclined to fix the income of the deceased @
Rs.8,000/- per month by interfering with the finding of the learned Tribunal.
21. It is also contended by the learned counsel for petitioners that the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded parental consortium to his minor child.

This Court, by relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others 1, is inclined to award a sum of Rs.40,000/- to his minor daughter i.e., petitioner No.3 in O.P. (2018) 18 SCC 130 MGP,J under the head of parental consortium and hereby calculate the compensation as detailed under:-
 S.No. Name of the Head Amount  awarded by  this Court  1 Monthly income Rs.8,000/-
 2. Addition of 40% Rs.11,200/-
 towards future  prospects as the  deceased being self-  employed and below  40 years

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the compensation arrived is more than the claim amount, it is pertinent to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case between Nagappa Vs.Gurudayal MGP,J Singh and others 2 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:-
"...under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (hereinafter referred to as "the MV Act") there is no restriction that compensation could be awarded only up to the amount claimed by the claimant.

entities.text: Nagappa Vs.Gurudayal MGP,J Singh and others 2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In an appropriate case where from the evidence brought on record if Tribunal/court considers that claimant is entitled to get more compensation than claimed, the Tribunal may pass such award.
Only embargo is it should be 'Just' compensation, that is to say, it should be neither arbitrary, fanciful nor unjustifiable from the evidence."
23. With the above finding of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, it is clear that the compensation can be granted more than the claim made based on cogent and convincing evidence.
24. In view of the above discussion and keeping in view the settled principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this Court deems fit and proper to allow the Appeal.

25. In the result, the Appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Trial Court from Rs.9,79,000/- to Rs.16,29,000/- which shall carry interest @ 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization AIR 2003 SC 674 MGP,J payable by respondent Nos.1, 3 to 5 jointly and severally within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Upon such deposit, the appellants are entitled to withdraw the same as per the apportionment made by the learned Tribunal by paying deficit Court fee.
There shall be no order as to costs.
26. Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
